Create a reproducible calibration/validation split

Source: R/nomo_split.R
nomo_split.Rd

nomo_split() creates an explicit random split for workflows in which EFA and CFA should be evaluated on different observations when the available sample permits it. The function does not claim that sample splitting is always preferable: dividing a modest sample reduces precision in both subsets, and an external validation sample is generally stronger evidence when one is available.

Usage

nomo_split(
  data,
  validation_prop = 0.5,
  seed = 1234L,
  guidance = nomo_defaults()
)

Arguments

data

A non-empty data frame.

validation_prop

Proportion of rows assigned to the validation sample. Must be strictly between 0 and 1.

seed

Integer seed used to make the split reproducible.

guidance

Guidance settings from nomo_defaults().

Value

A nomo_split object containing calibration, validation, a row-level assignment table, split sizes, the seed, and a decision log.

Details

The caller's random-number-generator state is restored after the split so that using nomo_split() does not silently alter later stochastic analyses.

Examples

split <- nomo_split(mtcars, validation_prop = 0.40, seed = 2026)
split
#> <nomo_split>
#> Rows: 32 total | 19 calibration | 13 validation
#> Validation proportion: 0.400 requested | 0.406 realized | Seed: 2026
#> Use splitting only when the gain in independence justifies the loss of precision.
nrow(split$calibration)
#> [1] 19
nrow(split$validation)
#> [1] 13
